answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: before an agent can earn, it locks a bond that is slashed if it misbehaves, so creating thousands of fake identities costs real capital every time. Honest reputation works like nectar that accumulates slowly through verified work, while basalt-hard collateral anchors each identity to something scarce. When many accounts share one funding source, peers can raise a violet flag and refuse to attest them, starving sybils of rewards without any central gatekeeper.
